subject: Janussi, Keeper of the Tome
fact: Janussi, Keeper of the Tome, was alive and eating dinner with an intact face and unchipped teeth before his death, and was murdered in the narrow window between that meal and the discovery of his body.
source_quote: Janussi had eaten dinner with his face intact and his teeth whole.

subject: desecration of Janussi's body
fact: Janussi's heart was torn out and ribcage smashed with precise, deliberate strokes after death, indicating the killer was not trying to kill but to desecrate the corpse at leisure.
source_quote: The heart was gone — torn out, not for any wound it would cause, but as a guard against any working that calls the dead back to answer.

subject: unknown poison substance
fact: A black, unidentified substance found on Janussi’s fingertip, lower lip, and tongue could not be recognized by Glabbagool, an ooze that has ingested countless Underdark materials, indicating it is a rare or unnatural poison.
source_quote: When even a creature that has eaten the Underdark can't place a poison, you've learned the poison is worth being afraid of.

subject: blackened fingertip and lip stain
fact: The black stain on Janussi’s fingertip and lower lip was not ink, but a darker, unidentifiable substance, suggesting he ingested it while reading — possibly as part of a magical or toxic mechanism tied to the text he was copying.
source_quote: The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was not.

subject: crime scene — Keeper’s chamber
fact: The crime scene contained a chipped tooth on the floor near the body, indicating Janussi fell face-first before death, and his body was later rolled onto his back by the killer.
source_quote: He had fallen forward. Face-first. Chipped the tooth on the way down. And then someone had come in, after, and rolled him onto his back to take the heart.

subject: broken nose
fact: Janussi’s nose was broken before death, as evidenced by bruising that cannot form on a corpse, placing the injury within the final moments of his life, prior to the heart removal.
source_quote: Bruising doesn't form on a corpse; there's no living tissue to swell.

subject: midnight blue ink stains on right sleeve
fact: Midnight blue ink stains on the right sleeve of Janussi’s tunic — the working hand — confirm he was actively taking notes at the time of death, suggesting he was interrupted while writing.
source_quote: Writing hand, fresh stains. A man interrupted at work.

subject: the reading poison mechanism
fact: The pattern of black substance on finger and lip suggests Janussi was wetting his fingertip to turn pages — and that the pages themselves may have been the source of the poison, implying a magical or sentient text that consumes those who read it.
source_quote: Turning pages, wetting the fingertip the way readers do without thinking, a hundred times an hour, never once considering that the page might be the thing reading them.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir identified the potential link between Glabbagool’s Underdark ingestion and the unidentifiable poison, providing the critical investigative angle that led to confirming the substance’s danger.
source_quote: Wouldn't Glabbagool have ingested, like, all sorts of different kinds of materials and poisons and goo in the Underdark?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum correctly determined the nose was broken pre-mortem by analyzing bruising patterns, and later confirmed the wound was cleanly inflicted, suggesting a skilled assailant.
source_quote: His read of the wound came clean — sharp work this time — and the nose had broken before death.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted the chipped tooth was a recent injury and questioned whether it was tied to the murder or a prior event, contributing to the logical separation of two possible narratives.
source_quote: So either that was related to him being murdered, immediately as part of the murder, or it was something we need to investigate — how did he chip the tooth recently?

subject: the identity of the killer
fact: The killer acted with calm precision, showed no urgency, and performed a ritualistic desecration — suggesting a person with intimate knowledge of magical protections and a motive beyond simple murder.
source_quote: Whoever did this had not been in a rush. He had not been trying to kill. He had been desecrating a corpse at his leisure, with nowhere to be.

subject: Candlekeep Scribes
fact: The use of midnight blue ink — the ink used in Candlekeep’s books — confirms Janussi was engaged in official transcription work, implicating the Archive’s internal practices or texts as potential sources of the threat.
source_quote: Wasn't the blue ink — the ink they used in the books?
